newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam comfortable with '97 EPS of $1.41.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam comfortable with '97 EPS of $1.41.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp chairman and chief executive Al Dunlap said Wednesday he is comfortable with Wall Street consensus earnings estimates of $1.41 per share for 1997 and $2.01 for 1998.
Dunlap also said in a telephone interview that he sees Sunbeam's sales doubling to about $2.0 billion in three years.
Earlier Wednesday, Sunbeam said second-quarter 1997 sales, excluding discontinued and divested operations, rose to $287.6 million, a 16.6 percent increase from a year ago on a comparable basis.
Earnings per share from continuing operations rose to $0.30 from $0.03 a year ago.

Noting it has been about one year since he arrived at Sunbeam as chief executive, Dunlap said he found the company "a total disaster" but in one year he achieved "a dramatic turnaround." He added, "We're now refining things; the restructuring is over."
Dunlap said he replaced various computer systems at Sunbeam with a new state-of-the-art system and reduced the number of factories from 26 to eight.

He said he got out of some lackluster businesses and opened up new distribution channels including overseas for remaining products. He said Sunbeam now exports electric blankets made at a factory in the U.S. to China.

He said his goal is to be debt free by the end of 1997. "I think the market would applaud a major acquisition" by Sunbeam, he said. He said an acquisition candidate would probably be a company with poor management but good brands.
